rationale: validation_report flags an uncovered_requirement issue for FR1: the FR1-targeting mutant (mutant_FR1_constant_change_wrong_table_value) went undetected by FR1's own check. Examining the mutant, it genuinely corrupts table entries at indices 3 and 5 (0xC4->0xC5, 0x92->0x93), which changes the observable return value of lookup() for the value/key combinations that map to idx==3 or idx==5. This is a real, observable functional defect -- the mutant's expected_detection description is accurate and matches what a proper exhaustive FR1 oracle comparison should catch. Since FR1's check is described as functionally identical to SR4's check (same harness invocation, same mismatch computation) and SR4 evidently DID catch this same corrupted table (mutation_score counts SR4 as passing/detecting since only FR1 is listed as uncovered), the FR1 check itself must be implemented with a narrower or non-exhaustive comparison (e.g., a small vector sample that happens to miss idx 3/5) rather than the full 65536-pair exhaustive oracle comparison the spec requires. This is an evaluation_framework bug: FR1's check.py logic is not exhaustively verifying all (value,key) pairs against the reference oracle as required by acceptance_criteria and FR1's own requirement text, even though SR4 (nominally testing the same property) apparently does catch it. Root cause is evaluation_issue, not mutation_issue, since the mutant is valid and should have been caught.
revision_instructions: The FR1 check in evaluate.py is not independently and exhaustively verifying functional correctness -- it failed to detect mutant_FR1_constant_change_wrong_table_value, which corrupts two table entries (at internal indices 3 and 5) causing wrong outputs for the (value,key) pairs that map to those indices. Rewrite the FR1 check so it compiles and runs the submission against a reference oracle computing table[(value^key)&0x0F] using the ORIGINAL unmodified 16-entry table shipped in inputs/, and exhaustively compares lookup(value,key) to that oracle for all 256x256 (value,key) pairs (or at minimum, includes dedicated probes for every one of the 16 possible idx values 0..15, ensuring corruption of any single table entry is observable). Do not rely on a small or non-exhaustive sample of (value,key) pairs for FR1 -- the check must FAIL whenever ANY table entry has been altered from its expected reference value, matched purely through the pinned lookup(value,key) interface and its return value, not by inspecting source text. Ensure FR1's oracle table matches the golden/shipped table contents exactly so a correct hardened submission (which preserves the table) still passes.
